pages.title: Setup and Testing
pages.text:
Congratulations on building your Gladly integration. Now, you can test the myriad possibilities of the Gladly API in a safe, secure space. This guide will help you understand the testing and iteration process.

## Sandbox environment

If you do not have a sandbox environment and are interested in purchasing one, please contact your Gladly CSM or Gladly Support team. Sandbox environments are a great way to test your code without impacting your production environment.

Your sandbox environment will be accessible via the URL below where `organization` is your company name.

```
https://{organization}.gladly.qa
```

## Set up API Users

Gladly Administrators can set API permissions on an Agent-by-Agent basis. We'll discuss how this maps to API access in the Authentication section below. Of course, the API User will also have access to Gladly overall.

To allow a user to create API tokens and access the API:

1. Log in to your **Gladly instance**.
2. Open the **menu** on the top left-hand corner of the page.
3. Navigate to **Settings > Users**.
4. Search and click the **user profile** that should have access.
5. You'll see a permission called **API User**. Select it, while keeping the user's Agent role intact.
6. Click **Save** to give access.

We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls whose account won't be used for Agent and organization management. This will help with future audits of API and agent activity.

## API tokens

You must create an API token to access Gladly API resources (see above).

### Create

If your profile already has access to the **API User** permission, you'll see a menu item titled Settings.

1. Click **Settings**.
2. Click **API tokens** then **Add Token** button on the upper right-hand corner of the page.
3. A token will be generated and named **New Token** by default.

   * If you have **existing tokens**, it might be named New Token 2, New Token 3, etc.
4. Click the name to **rename**.

You will only see a new token once before you navigate away from the page. This token will be associated with your Agent profile.

### Replace and Rotate

If you lose this token or it is time to rotate your application keys:

1. **Generate** a new token.
2. **Store** the new token in a secure location.
3. **Delete** the old token.
4. **Update** your applications and scripts with the new token.

## Authentication

Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication. API tokens are associated with designated Gladly users. Your user must have the API user permission to create and use an API token. An API token can be used to perform any API request without restriction.

The credentials must be passed via an Authorization HTTP header. All requests must be made over HTTPS.

Users assigned the **Team Manager** or **Administrator** roles can contact Gladly Support. Log into Gladly as one of these roles, clickon the top-left corner, then click **Contact Gladly Support**. Gladly Support's primary operating hours are Monday through Friday, 6 AM to 6 PM Pacific Time, but you can submit a request anytime.

* Please select the correct business impact (P1 to P4).
* Most requests should be sent as a P4.

pages.title: Get Your API tokens
pages.text:
## Background

API tokens are required to use the Gladly APIs for security and authentication purposes. These can be created within the Gladly UI, for users who have the `API User` role.

## Goals

Have at least one technical admin log in to Gladly and create a token.

## Estimated Effort

15 minutes

## Step-by-Step Tutorial & Best Practices

1. Log in to Gladly.
2. Click the menu icon on the top left, then click **Settings**.
3. Under **App Developer Tools**, click on **API token**.
4. Click **Create Token**. A new token is immediately generated within the page.
5. Add a meaningful name to the token (optional). This is for reference only.

pages.title: Generate API Tokens and Create Webhooks
pages.text:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **REQUIRED USER ROLE** API User | **PERMISSION OVERVIEW** View permissions by role |

API tokens are required to use Gladly APIs for security and authentication purposes. Tokens can be accessed and created by users who at least have an API user role.

## Before you start

* For integrations not built by Gladly, a Gladly Administrator should create a new user with an API role + Agent and/or Administrator (check with your integration partner to confirm the required roles) account for *each* integration. This account should be used to access Gladly to create the API tokens or webhooks.

  + The integration partner should provide the email address to be used with the integration's user account in Gladly. They must also access emails from this account to activate their Gladly account to create API tokens or webhooks.
* API tokens are tied to a single user account and a particular environment. For example, an API token attached to Gladly user *developer@customer.com* in the Sandbox environment is not valid for *developer@customer.com* in the Production environment.

  + We recommend creating a dedicated Gladly user to make API calls whose account won't be used for Agent and organization management. This will help you with any future audits of API activity vs. Agent activity.

## Create a unique user account linked to webhooks or tokens

1. As an Administrator, create a user to use explicitly to create and attach webhooks or tokens.

   * Be sure to add the user with at least an API User role + Agent and/or Administrator. If this user needs access to reports, they'll need Administrator access. For a complete list of user permissions, click here.
   * **Note –** We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls.

     + Use the email address provided by the integration partner if you're given one.
   * Use a name to help you quickly identify the integration user. For example, "Retale Integration."
2. An email will be sent to the user. Someone must complete the registration and sign in to Gladly to create API tokens or webhooks. They'll have 24 hours to accept the user invitation before it expires.

   * See How do I reset my password for login issues.
   * For SSO users, see Manager Users through SSO for more information.

> Deactivating an API User
>
> If a user account with API tokens or webhooks attached to it is deactivated, apps or external sources using the token or webhook linked to the user will stop working.

## Create API tokens

1. Click  on the top left corner of the screen.
2. Click **Settings**.
3. Under the **App Developer Tools** category, click **API tokens**. The API tokens page will show you a list of currently available API tokens.
4. Click **Create Token**.
5. A new token is immediately generated within the page.

* Copy and secure the token under the Token column. **The token is only shown once**, so save it in a secure location.
* Click the token name (e.g., Token 1) to rename the token to make it easy to identify how the token is used.
* To delete a token, hover over the token and click .

## Create new webhooks

Create up to 50 webhooks for your organization. See our developer guide for more information about webhooks.

1. Click  on the top left corner of the screen.
2. Click **Settings**.
3. Under the **App Developer Tools** category, click **Webhooks**. The Webhooks page will show you a list of webhooks you currently have configured.
4. Click **Create Webhook**.
5. From the Create Webhook page, enter the following information:

   * **Name –** Enter a name to help you identify the app using a webhook.
   * **Enabled (toggle) –** Allows you to activate/deactivate the webhook. Click the toggle so it's green to activate the webhook.
   * **Webhook URL –** Enter the URL where you'd like to send events.

     + If you get an "unable to ping URL" error, double-check the URL and make sure it's correct.
   * **Events –** Select the events you'd like to use from the search picklist. The Webhook Events you select are added below the search bar. For more information about Webhook Events, please visit our developer guide.
   * **Username (Optional) –** Enter the username for the app you are integrating.
   * **Password (Optional) –** Enter the password for the app you are integrating.
   * **Realm (Optional) –** Enter realm to run basic auth against.
   * **HTTP Headers (Optional) –** There are two columns (Header, Value) required for HTTP Headers (e.g., X-API-Key) to be included in every request.

     + Click **Add a Header** to add a new line.
     + Click  to delete a line.
6. Click **Save**. This will take you back to the Webhooks page, where the webhook you just added is visible.

### Activate/Deactivate a webhook

In the **Status** column, click the toggle next to the webhook you want to activate/deactivate. The toggle turns gray when it's deactivated and green when activated.

#### Reactivate a webhook

Gladly automatically deactivates webhooks that fail. To see when a webhook was deactivated, hover over the **exclamation point**. Once the issue causing the webhook to fail is resolved, reactivate it. If the webhook is not being used, keep it deactivated or delete it if it is no longer used.

### Delete a webhook

To delete a webhook, hover over the webhook and click .

## Replace or rotate API tokens

Should you lose this token or wish to rotate your application keys, you can do the following:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Store the new token in a secure location.
3. Delete the old token.
4. Update your applications/scripts with the new token.

### App Platform

Build integrations with external systems to take action and
retrieve data.

* Learn more

### REST API

Integrate seamlessly with Gladly by enabling a connector,
calling Gladly's REST APIs, or implementing the Lookup
API to provide data from your own services.

* Learn more

### Chat SDK

Embed Chat SDK in your website or app to let customers
search for answers or contact your customer service team.

* Web
* iOS
* Android

### Help Center

Help your customers help themselves. Use this reference to
configure the answers your customers see on your Help
Center, styled the way you want it.

* Learn more

### Tutorials

Learn how to use our APIs to automate popular workflows
ranging from exporting conversation data out of Gladly to
building integrations with 3rd party providers.

* Learn more

### Code Examples

Explore sample code and reference implementations for
Gladly's APIs, webhooks, and platform tools.

Some implementation packages include a Sandbox environment. If it does, you'll have access to an environment with an address like acme.gladly.qa.

This environment is used typically for development and testing purposes. For example, if we release a new feature to Sandbox, you'll have the opportunity to test the feature without interrupting your Production environment where Agents are actively helping Customers.

## Key TakeAways

* Sandbox and Production environment are not connected. If you add users to Sandbox, they are not transferred to Production.
* Sometimes, Sandbox is also used to do basic training in a non-production environment.
* Configurations cannot be exported to Production from Sandbox. They are both stand-alone environments unless specified in your SOW as a one-time activity.
* Test new features in Sandbox (if you have one) to prevent configuration mishaps in Production.

Connect Gladly AI to an external MCP server so it can call that server's tools during Customer conversations. This article covers adding and testing a connection, then using its tools in a Guide. To learn how MCP connections work, see What are MCP connections?

> MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill.
>
> Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply.

## Before you begin

Have the following ready for the MCP server you want to connect:

* The server URL, for example `https://api.example.com/mcp`
* The type of authentication the server uses: none, bearer token, API key, or OAuth (authorization code or client credentials)
* The credentials for that authentication type

## Access MCP settings

1. Go to **Settings**.
2. Under **App Developer Tools**, select **MCP**.

The **MCP** page lists your connections on the **Active** and **Inactive** tabs. For each connection, the table shows the connection name, the server, its success rate, and its status.

MCP page with no connections configured.

If you haven't added a connection yet, the page prompts you to add one.

## Add a connection to a new MCP server

1. On the **MCP** page, select **Add Connection**.
2. Select the **Server** dropdown, then select **+ New MCP server**.
3. Enter the **Server URL**.
4. Enter a **Server name** that helps your team recognize the server, for example "Retalè Footwear".
5. Select an **Authentication** type:

   * **None**
   * **Bearer Token**
   * **API Key**
   * **OAuth (Authorization Code)**
   * **OAuth (Client Credentials)**
6. Enter the credentials for the authentication type you selected. For OAuth (Authorization Code), a sign-in window opens so you can authorize the connection.
7. (Optional) Enter a **Description**, for example "Store information, order status lookups, and product catalog search".
8. Enter a **Connection name**, for example "retale-footwear".
9. Keep **Active** turned on if you want the connection available right away.
10. Select **Save**.

When the connection is saved, the **Connection Added** page confirms that the connection is saved. Select **Test Tools** to try one of the server's tools right away, or select **Done** to return to the **MCP** page.

### Add another connection to an existing server

If your org already has a server registered, you can create another connection to it, for example to use different credentials.

1. On the **MCP** page, select **Add Connection**.
2. Select the **Server** dropdown and choose a server under **Your servers**. You can search by name or URL.
3. Enter a **Connection name**.
4. Keep **Active** turned on if you want the connection available right away.
5. Select **Save**.

## Test the MCP

You have two test options: **Test Connection** checks that Gladly can reach the server and find its tools, and **Test Tool** runs one tool so you can review its output.

> What is a tool?
>
> In MCP, a tool is a single action an external server lets Gladly AI run, such as looking up an order or searching a product catalog. Each tool has a name, a description, and the inputs it needs, and it returns a result that Gladly AI can use in its reply. One MCP server can offer many tools, and Gladly discovers them automatically when you add a connection.
>
> Examples from a footwear store’s server:
>
> * `lookup_order_status`: takes an order number and returns the order’s status and tracking details.
> * `search_products`: takes a search phrase, such as “loafers”, and returns matching products with prices and sizes.
> * `get_store_hours`: takes no inputs and returns the store’s hours.

### Test a connection

Test a connection to confirm that Gladly can reach the server and discover its tools.

1. On the **MCP** page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row.
2. Select **Test Connection**.

A confirmation banner appears with the number of tools Gladly found on the server, for example "Connected - 3 tools available".

### Test a tool

Run a tool on its own to see what it returns, before you add it to a Guide or Skill.

1. On the **MCP** page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row, then select **Test Tool**.
2. Select the **Tool** dropdown and choose the tool you want to run. You can search the list by name. **Run** stays unavailable until you select a tool.
3. Review the tool's description and the **Input schema** at the bottom of the page. Required fields are marked **REQUIRED**. Select **Required only** to hide optional fields, or **Copy** to copy the schema.
4. Fill in the fields. For inputs that aren't simple text, such as arrays, select **Edit as JSON**. If the tool takes no inputs, an **Arguments (JSON)** box appears with `{}` in it. Leave it as is.
5. Select **Run**.

The result appears under **Run**, labeled **Success** when the call works. Select **Copy** to copy the result.

> If you leave a required field empty, the tool call fails.
>
> Check the **Input schema** to confirm which fields the tool requires.

## Manage the MCP

### View tool call logs

Tool call logs show each time a tool ran, including test runs.

1. On the **MCP** page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row.
2. Select **View Logs**.
3. Select a log entry to expand it. Each entry shows the tool name, the date and time of the call, and a green check mark if the call succeeded.
4. Select the **Request** tab to see the request URL, method, header keys, and payload. Select the **Response** tab to see the response information, header keys, and body. The time the call took appears at the top right.

### Edit, deactivate, or delete a connection

From the menu at the end of a connection's row, you can:

* Select **Edit** to update the connection.
* Select **Deactivate** to take the connection offline without deleting it. Deactivated connections move to the **Inactive** tab.
* Select **Delete** to remove the connection.

---

## Use MCP tools in conversations

To make an MCP tool available to Gladly AI in a Guide, wrap the tool in a Custom Action, then add that Action to a Guide section. The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps. The examples below use a product search tool, `search_products`, on a faux company MCP server.

### Create a Custom Action that calls an MCP tool

#### Create a Custom Action

1. #### Go to **Settings**. Under **App Developer Tools**, select **Custom Actions**.
2. Select **Add App Action**.
3. Enter a **Name** and a **Description**. Gladly uses these to decide when to run the Action, so describe what the Action does, what input it needs, and what it returns.
4. Under **Inputs**, select **Add** and enter the information Gladly AI needs to collect from the customer:

   * **Name:** A descriptive name in snake\_case or camelCase, for example `query`.
   * **Description:** What the input represents and how it should be formatted, for example "The customer's shoe search, such as a style, color, or category (loafers, boots, sneakers, sandals)".
   * **Type:** Select the data type, for example **String**.
   * **Input required:** Select this if the Action can't run without the input.
5. Add (+ icon) and configure a **Tool** step:

   * **Name:** A name for the step in snake\_case or camelCase, for example `searchProducts`.
   * **Configuration:** Select your MCP connection.
   * **Tool:** Select the MCP tool to run. The tool's description appears below the dropdown.
   * **Required Parameters:** Map each tool parameter to an Action input by entering `$.params.` followed by the input name. For example, enter `$.params.query` for the `query` parameter.
6. Select **Save**. New Actions are saved as **Inactive**.

#### Test the Action

1. In the Action editor, select **Test**.
2. In the **Test inputs** window, optionally imitate a customer, set the **Channel Type**, set **Is Authenticated**, and enter a **Gladly Agent ID** or **Conversation ID**.
3. Enter a value for each Action input, for example "boots" for `query`.
4. Select **Test**.

#### Set the Action to active

An Action must be active before you can use it in a Guide.

1. On the **Custom Actions** page, select the **Inactive** tab.
2. Select the menu at the end of the Action's row, then select **Set to active**.
3. In the **Set as active** window, select **Set as active**. Any recent changes are saved and become available in Guides and App Actions.

From the same menu, you can select **Edit**, **View logs**, or **Duplicate**.

### Apply the Action to a Guide

#### Add the Custom Action to a Guide

1. Open your AI Agent, then select **Add Guide**, or open an existing Guide.
2. Enter a name and a short description for the Guide.
3. In a section, enter a heading and a description of when to use it, for example "Use this when a customer asks about shoes, styles, colors, sizes, prices, or availability."
4. Keep **Action** selected, then select the **Select Action** dropdown. You can search by name.
5. Select your Action. It appears in the list with a **
